context.process_name: Due From Funds & Portfolio Companies Billing
context.objective: Document how we carry out Due From Funds & Portfolio Companies Billing, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we open the billing cycle and prepare both workbooks. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: record the billing period and populations; copy the prior fund workbook and portfolio-company workbook into the current-cycle location; update period references; for portfolio companies update the “One Rock Capital Partners Transaction Report” header on all approximately 25–27 tabs; confirm fund tabs, affiliate tabs, portfolio-company tabs, Notes tab, formulas, and pivots are present. Next, we pull and clean fund general-ledger activity. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: run Sage GL for accounts 1101–1105, the full billing period, with the applicable location filter; export to Excel, wrap text, and remove merge/center formatting; add a net column equal to debit minus credit, fill through every account section, paste as values, and remove original debit/credit columns; remove all document-number rows beginning with Invoice ; sum remaining transactions by account and compare to the Sage ending balance.
What do you do if the summed transactions don’t match the Sage ending balance?

After that, we populate and reconcile main-fund tabs. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: add required blank rows to each fund tab; copy transaction dates through net amount; do not copy Sage running balances; remove unused rows and extend running-balance/sum formulas; confirm each tab agrees with its “Per Sage” amount; leave the general-ledger coding column blank for the internal fund team; mark completed account sections in the source workpaper so they are not processed twice. Then, we populate and reconcile affiliates. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: pull the full Due From Affiliates account with no customer filter and clean it using Step 2; build a pivot with Customer Name as rows and Transaction Amount as values; exclude GP entities, old funds no longer billed, and out-of-population entities only under confirmed population rules; populate each affiliate tab; run a separate Sage report for each affiliate or customer and confirm the tab agrees with it.
When a cleaned account total doesn’t match the Sage ending balance, what do you do to resolve it?

Once that is done, we assemble fund and affiliate supporting documents. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: sort detail by document number; retrieve invoice PDFs and allocation support from the cited Box vendor folders; retrieve GJ support from Sage or email and credit/refund support from email; store support in one consolidated cycle folder because items can affect multiple entities; cross-reference support to workbook lines. Following that, we complete fund/affiliate review and client approval. That is done by: Preparer, GPFS reviewer, internal fund team, One Rock. What we do: the GPFS reviewer checks Sage reconciliations and unusual items or missing support; the internal fund team reviews the package, completes the applicable general-ledger coding, and records questions on the Notes tab; preparer resolves internal notes and sends client questions as needed; place the package in the Client Collaboration folder and notify One Rock; record One Rock email feedback, update the workbook, and repeat review until final approval.
How do you prepare and reconcile the portfolio-company billing tabs?

Following that, we create fund and affiliate accounts-receivable invoices and hand off payment requests. That is done by: GPFS preparer; internal fund team/Treasury downstream. What we do: create accounts-receivable invoices in Sage, either individually by updating a prior invoice or through an approved bulk import; date each invoice the first day of the month after period end; use reference Q[#]/[Year] ; mirror the memo to the reference; print each invoice and save using entity name, invoice number, and amount; complete internal invoice review and send the package to the fund team; the fund team sends the payment request to Treasury. GPFS asks to receive copies of payment notifications so the received cash can be matched to the correct invoice. Following that, we pull, clean, and split portfolio-company general-ledger activity. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: run the Sage general-ledger report for account 1201, using the quarter date range and no customer or location filter; clean the report using Step 2. Also remove the department column and the 1201 summary header row; remove prior Invoice rows; build a Customer Name / Transaction Amount pivot; identify and exclude approved write-offs/out-of-population entities.
What do you do with the remaining portfolio-company activity after identifying and excluding those entities?

Following that, we resolve parent/add-on mappings and populate entity tabs. That is done by: GPFS preparer. What we do: for every add-on/holding customer, inspect Sage AR > Customer > Additional Information > Parent ; combine add-on activity with its parent tab. Examples: Pros DCI → Port EnviroServe; Comfort Investor Holdings → Port Comfort; Island Energy Investor Holdings → Port IES; paste current rows into the correct entity tab; update formulas; refresh the expense-type pivot (filing, audit, accounting, legal, meals, travel, technology, other); run a separate Sage 1201 report for each customer or parent population and confirm the tab agrees with it. Following that, we preserve and exclude “Do Not Bill” items correctly. That is done by: GPFS preparer; reviewer. What we do: keep Do Not Bill items in aggregate detail so the Sage reconciliation remains complete; exclude those items from billable totals; record the classification and confirm the aggregate total still agrees with Sage.
What determines whether a portfolio-company item is classified as “Do Not Bill”?

Following that, we complete portfolio-company review and produce deal-team files. That is done by: Same review chain; GPFS preparer produces files. What we do: complete the GPFS, internal fund-team, and One Rock reviews described in Step 6; after approval, create one Excel per portfolio company for deal-team review; include current-quarter expenses only; remove historical activity and historical Do Not Bill items from the deal-team file; preserve the complete current-quarter expense-type pivot; save individual files in the separate approved portfolio-company folder. Following that, we update the Expense Tracker. That is done by: GPFS preparer; One Rock reviews. What we do: enter billable amount per entity and grand total; update previously reimbursed amounts, accrued/credit balances, bank reserves, net amount, prior-quarter comparison, and deal-team approval status; confirm the net amount agrees with Sage; confirm the meaning of “accrued balance” versus “credit” with One Rock.
What prompts the preparer to open a billing cycle?

Following that, we create portfolio-company accounts-receivable invoices and route reserve payments. That is done by: GPFS preparer; Treasury for reserve-funded entities. What we do: map detailed expense classes to Professional Fees, Other Expenses, Meals, and Travel; prove grouped classes equal the approved billable amount by entity; prepare the bulk import (approximately 100 lines is a source example) or approved manual invoices; review each imported invoice individually and confirm it remains one page; route reserve-funded entity invoices directly to Treasury for payment from reserves; route all others through the standard approved payment chain.
What does Treasury do after receiving an invoice for a reserve-funded entity?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

notes.summary: The preparer groups portfolio-company expenses, ties them to approved billable amounts and prepares invoices by bulk import or approved manual entry. Reserve-funded invoices go directly to Treasury; others follow the standard approved payment chain.

After preparing the workbooks, a GPFS preparer pulls and cleans fund general-ledger activity. The preparer runs Sage GL for accounts 1101–1105 for the full billing period with the applicable location filter, exports to Excel, wraps text, removes merge/center formatting, adds a net column equal to debit minus credit and fills it through every account section, pastes the results as values, removes the original debit/credit columns, and removes document-number rows beginning with “Invoice.”
The GPFS preparer populates each main-fund tab by adding blank rows and copying transaction dates through net amount, excluding Sage running balances. The preparer removes unused rows, extends running-balance and sum formulas, confirms each tab agrees with its “Per Sage” amount, leaves the GL coding column blank for the internal fund team, and marks completed account sections in the source workpaper to prevent duplicate processing.
For affiliates, the GPFS preparer pulls the full Due From Affiliates account without a customer filter and cleans it using the earlier GL-cleanup step. The preparer builds a pivot with Customer Name as rows and Transaction Amount as values, excludes specified entities only under confirmed population rules, populates each affiliate tab, and runs a separate Sage report for each affiliate or customer to confirm agreement.
After populating and reconciling affiliates, the GPFS preparer sorts fund and affiliate detail by document number, retrieves invoice PDFs and allocation support from cited Box vendor folders, GJ support from Sage or email, and credit/refund support from email. The preparer stores support in one consolidated cycle folder because items can affect multiple entities, and cross-references it to workbook lines.
Following support assembly, the GPFS reviewer checks reconciliations and unusual items or missing support. The internal fund team reviews the package, completes applicable GL coding and records questions on the Notes tab; the preparer resolves internal notes and sends client questions as needed.
The package is placed in the Client Collaboration folder and One Rock is notified. One Rock email feedback is recorded, the workbook updated, and review repeated until final approval; the participant did not specify who performs each of these actions.
Following fund and affiliate approval, the GPFS preparer creates accounts-receivable invoices in Sage, either by updating a prior invoice individually or through an approved bulk import. Each is dated the first day of the month after period end, uses reference Q[#]/[Year] and the same memo, and is printed and saved using entity name, invoice number and amount.
After internal invoice review, the package is sent to the fund team, which sends the payment request to Treasury. GPFS asks for copies of payment notifications so received cash can be matched to the correct invoice.
Following the fund and affiliate invoice handoff, the GPFS preparer runs Sage GL for account 1201 for the quarter date range without customer or location filters. The preparer cleans it using the earlier cleanup, removes the department column, 1201 summary header and prior Invoice rows, builds a Customer Name / Transaction Amount pivot, and identifies and excludes approved write-offs and out-of-population entities.

The preparer pastes current rows into the correct entity tab, updates formulas, refreshes the expense-type pivot and compares the tab with a separate Sage 1201 report for each customer or parent population.
The preparer and reviewer preserve Do Not Bill items in aggregate detail for Sage reconciliation but exclude them from billable totals, record the classification and confirm the aggregate still agrees with Sage.
Portfolio-company work follows the GPFS, internal fund-team and One Rock review chain. After approval, the GPFS preparer creates one Excel file per portfolio company for deal-team review, including current-quarter expenses only, removing historical activity and historical Do Not Bill items, retaining the complete current-quarter expense-type pivot, and saving each file in the separate approved portfolio-company folder.
The GPFS preparer updates the Expense Tracker with billable amounts per entity and grand total, previously reimbursed amounts, accrued or credit balances, bank reserves, net amount, prior-quarter comparison and deal-team approval status. One Rock reviews, and the net amount is checked against Sage.
After updating the Expense Tracker, the GPFS preparer maps detailed expense classes to Professional Fees, Other Expenses, Meals and Travel and proves the grouped classes equal each entity's approved billable amount. The preparer prepares a bulk import or approved manual invoices and reviews each imported invoice individually for a one-page format.
Portfolio-company invoices for reserve-funded entities are routed directly to Treasury for payment from reserves; all others go through the standard approved payment chain.

steps.title: Open cycle and prepare workbooks
steps.description: Record the billing period and populations. Copy the prior fund and portfolio-company workbooks to the current-cycle location and update period references. Update the One Rock Capital Partners Transaction Report header on approximately 25–27 portfolio-company tabs. Confirm fund, affiliate, portfolio-company and Notes tabs, formulas and pivots are present.

steps.title: Pull and clean fund activity
steps.description: Run Sage GL for accounts 1101–1105 for the full billing period with the applicable location filter. Export to Excel, wrap text and remove merge/center formatting. Add net as debit minus credit throughout every account section, paste as values and remove the original debit and credit columns. Remove document-number rows beginning with Invoice. Sum remaining transactions by account and compare with the Sage ending balance.

steps.title: Populate and reconcile fund tabs
steps.description: Add required blank rows and copy transaction dates through net amount, but not Sage running balances. Remove unused rows and extend running-balance and sum formulas. Confirm each tab agrees with its Per Sage amount. Leave the GL coding column blank for the internal fund team and mark completed account sections in the source workpaper so they are not processed twice.

steps.title: Prepare and reconcile affiliates
steps.description: Pull the full Due From Affiliates account without a customer filter and clean it using the fund GL method in S2. Build a pivot with Customer Name as rows and Transaction Amount as values. Exclude GP entities, old funds no longer billed and out-of-population entities only under confirmed population rules. Populate each affiliate tab, run a separate Sage report for each affiliate or customer and confirm the tab agrees.

steps.title: Assemble fund billing support
steps.system: Box; Sage; email; consolidated cycle folder
steps.description: Sort fund and affiliate detail by document number. Retrieve invoice PDFs and allocation support from cited Box vendor folders, GJ support from Sage or email, and credit/refund support from email. Store support in one consolidated cycle folder because items can affect multiple entities, and cross-reference it to workbook lines.

steps.title: Review fund and affiliate package
steps.actor: GPFS reviewer; internal fund team; preparer
steps.description: The GPFS reviewer checks Sage reconciliations and unusual items or missing support. The internal fund team reviews the package, completes applicable GL coding and records questions on the Notes tab. The preparer resolves internal notes and sends client questions as needed. Detailed handling of individual findings is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Handle One Rock feedback
steps.actor: Individual placement, notification, feedback-recording and workbook-update roles UNKNOWN
steps.description: Place the package in the Client Collaboration folder and notify One Rock. Record One Rock email feedback and update the workbook. The participant names the preparer, GPFS reviewer, internal fund team and One Rock for the overall review, but does not assign these individual actions.

steps.title: Repeat fund package review
steps.actor: Review participants and individual assignments on each repeat UNKNOWN
steps.description: Repeat review until final approval. Which review levels repeat, how further feedback is handled and where approval is retained are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Create fund and affiliate invoices
steps.description: Create accounts-receivable invoices individually by updating a prior invoice or through an approved bulk import. Date each invoice the first day of the month after period end, use reference Q[#]/[Year] and mirror that reference in the memo. Print each invoice and save it using entity name, invoice number and amount. Route-selection and import-approval details are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review and send invoice package
steps.actor: Internal invoice reviewer UNKNOWN; GPFS preparer reported for the overall invoice work
steps.description: Complete internal invoice review and send the package to the fund team. The individual reviewer and sender, checks, evidence and failure handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Send fund payment request
steps.actor: Internal fund team; GPFS requests notification copies
steps.description: The fund team sends the payment request to Treasury. GPFS asks to receive copies of payment notifications so received cash can be matched to the correct invoice. The timing of that request, notification receipt and actual matching are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Clean portfolio-company activity
steps.description: Run Sage GL for account 1201 for the quarter, without customer or location filters. Clean it using the fund GL method in S2, also removing the department column and 1201 summary header row and prior Invoice rows. Build a Customer Name / Transaction Amount pivot and identify and exclude approved write-offs and out-of-population entities.

steps.title: Map and reconcile company tabs
steps.description: For every add-on or holding customer, inspect Sage AR > Customer > Additional Information > Parent and combine its activity with the parent tab. Reported examples are Pros DCI to Port EnviroServe, Comfort Investor Holdings to Port Comfort, and Island Energy Investor Holdings to Port IES. Paste current rows into the correct entity tab, update formulas and refresh the expense-type pivot for filing, audit, accounting, legal, meals, travel, technology and other. Run a separate Sage 1201 report for each customer or parent population and confirm its tab agrees.

steps.title: Handle Do Not Bill items
steps.actor: GPFS preparer and reviewer; individual assignments UNKNOWN
steps.description: Keep Do Not Bill items in aggregate detail so the Sage reconciliation remains complete, exclude them from billable totals, record the classification and confirm the aggregate total still agrees with Sage. Classification criteria are UNKNOWN.

Include current-quarter expenses only; remove historical activity and historical Do Not Bill items; preserve the complete current-quarter expense-type pivot. topics.answer: The intake calls the work Due From Funds & Portfolio Companies Billing. It includes fund, affiliate and portfolio-company billing; other team or system names and the precise boundary are UNKNOWN.
The work produces reviewed billing packages, invoices and payment handoffs for funds, affiliates and portfolio companies. The ultimate delivered result and completion boundary are UNKNOWN.

The first reported action is opening a billing cycle and preparing workbooks. The actual initiating event, detector, upstream readiness and cadence are UNKNOWN. Portfolio activity uses a quarter range; fund invoices are dated the first day of the month after period end, an invoice date rather than an established processing deadline.

The fund team sends a payment request to Treasury; reserve-funded company invoices go directly to Treasury and other company invoices to a standard approved payment chain. Treasury processing, cash matching, deal-team completion and the observable finish of the overall work are UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN: overall accountability. The GPFS preparer performs much of the work, but performance does not establish accountability.

The preparer opens the cycle, copies and checks workbooks, cleans and reconciles Sage fund and affiliate activity, and assembles support. The GPFS reviewer and internal fund team review the package; One Rock feedback is recorded, the workbook updated and review repeated to final approval. Fund invoices are created and reviewed before the fund team requests payment. Portfolio activity is cleaned, mapped to parent tabs and reconciled; Do Not Bill items stay in aggregate detail but not billable totals. After the reported review and approval, the preparer creates deal-team files, updates the tracker and prepares invoices for reserve or other payment routing. Precise handoffs, correction routes, tracker-review dependency and final closure remain UNKNOWN.

Checks include workbook presence, Sage comparisons, confirmed affiliate population exclusions, reviewer checks of reconciliations and unusual or missing support, internal coding and One Rock review to final approval. Portfolio checks retain Do Not Bill detail in aggregate, compare tracker net to Sage, prove invoice groupings and check each imported invoice remains one page. Review evidence, thresholds, segregation, overrides, detailed rejection and rework handling, and tracker-review blocking are UNKNOWN.

Fund invoices may be created from prior invoices or an approved bulk import. Portfolio invoices use a bulk import or approved manual route; reserve-funded entities go directly to Treasury while others use the standard approved payment chain. Reasons, route-selection authority, effort, charging and removal constraints are UNKNOWN. No general GPFS standard is independently corroborated.

The participant describes copying and updating workbooks, cleaning exported activity, collecting support and updating the tracker. Whether these activities cause particular friction or extra effort is UNKNOWN; no pain point or effort estimate was reported.

The participant reports marking completed account sections so they are not processed twice and requesting payment notifications so cash can be matched to the correct invoice. Other failure consequences and their materiality are UNKNOWN.

Prior workbooks, invoice PDFs, allocation and general-journal support, email feedback and the Expense Tracker were mentioned. No procedure or other supporting document was supplied for independent review; availability and location of governing instructions are UNKNOWN.

The account covers funds, affiliates and portfolio companies, including add-on or holding customers and parent tabs. One Rock participates in review. Whether the route is client-specific or general GPFS practice, its parent process and entity-wide applicability are UNKNOWN.

Reported practices include net debit minus credit, removing Invoice rows, confirmed affiliate population exclusions, parent mapping from Sage, Do Not Bill treatment, invoice date and reference conventions, and expense-class grouping. Written sources, interpreters, conflict authority, approval basis, rounding and tracker calculations are UNKNOWN; no document was reviewed to verify these rules.

Sage supplies GL activity and customer parent information; the internal fund team reviews and codes, then sends fund payment requests to Treasury. Deal teams are intended to review company files, One Rock reviews packages and the tracker, and Treasury receives reserve-funded invoices. Upstream cycle initiation and downstream payment, approval and closure dependencies remain UNKNOWN.

Sage supplies GL, customer information and fund invoice creation; activity is exported to Excel and worked in copied workbooks. Box, Sage and email provide support stored in a consolidated cycle folder; Client Collaboration holds packages; company files go to a separate approved folder and the Expense Tracker is updated. Authoritative records, exact locations, workbook logic ownership and detailed tracker inputs are UNKNOWN.
